samples.summary: Shared spreadsheet viewer still publishes presence on mount and on every cursor move — under the new enforce-by-default posture this is the rw PushPull that gets 403'd, wedging the viewer's sync
samples.evidence: This change flips the auth webhook to enforcing by default and, on that premise, silences presence publishing on read-only mounts for board (`board-view.tsx:602`), slides (`slides-view.tsx:1137`), PDF (`pdf-collab.tsx:134`) and notes (`readOnlyNoteStore` neuters `setLocalSelection`). The spreadsheet surface was not covered. `SheetView` is mounted read-only for a viewer share link (`shared-document.tsx:283` passes `readOnly`), and `sheet-view.tsx:1012` constructs `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId)` unconditionally; the constructor immediately runs `this.doc.update((_, p) => p.set({ activeTabId: this.tabId }))` (yorkie-store.ts:86-88). `YorkieStore.updateSelection` (line 628) does the same on every cursor move, and it is called unconditionally from the engine (`packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3045,3058` in `syncSelectionToPresence`, which `setActiveCell` calls). By this PR's own reasoning (`pdf-collab.tsx:124-131`, `slides-view.tsx:1130-1136`) a presence `doc.update()` is a local change the next `PushPull` carries with verb `rw`, which the webhook refuses for a share-link `viewer` — so on any deployment that registers `PushPull` and configures nothing else (now the default), a viewer opening a shared sheet is permission-denied on its first sync. Note also `sheet.ts:3029` calls `store.ensureAxisOrder(...)` from the same presence sync, which can write the document root (rowOrder/colOrder) from a viewer.
searchedFor: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts (only for query results, not share viewers)

samples.summary: Shared docs viewer publishes cursor presence through the RAW (unwrapped) store on every cursor move and every remote change — same rw-PushPull denial the PR fixed for board/slides/pdf/notes
samples.evidence: `readOnlyDocStore` is applied only inside the engine (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075`), so it guards the editor's own writes. `docs-view.tsx` keeps the unwrapped `YorkieDocStore` (line 356) and calls presence mutators on it with no `readOnly` check: `store.updateCursorPos(pos, sel)` at lines 457 and 465 (registered unconditionally at line 452 via `editor.onCursorMove`), and `store.publishResolvedLocalCursor({...})` at line 433, which runs on *every* remote change. Both end in `p.set(...)` inside `doc.update` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1241, 3147). `SharedDocsLayout` mounts `DocsView` with `readOnly` for a viewer share link. With enforcement now the default, the first cursor move (or the first peer edit) makes the viewer's next `PushPull` carry a change → verb `rw` → 403 → the viewer's sync is wedged, which is exactly the failure the PR's own comments cite for the other four surfaces.
searchedFor: grep readOnlyDocStore across packages/frontend/src and packages/docs/src

samples.summary: Checked-in compiled JS copies of two ops scripts still attach with no auth token
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.js:138-139` and `packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.js:96` are compiled duplicates of the two `.ts` scripts this change updated, and they construct their clients without `authTokenInjector`. Anyone running the `.js` (they are in the repo; `copy-yorkie-documents` has no package.json script entry at all, so it is invoked by path) attaches anonymously and is denied wherever the webhook methods are registered — now the default posture. The `.ts` fix does not reach them.

samples.summary: Divider drag ratio divides by a track width that can be 0, producing NaN/Infinity flex values
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` (line 544) then `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;`. When the container is degenerate (jsdom `rect.width === 0`, or a container no wider than the now-25px divider) `track` is 0 or negative: `0/0` is NaN, and `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` is NaN, so `editorEl.style.flex = '1 1 NaN%'` — an invalid declaration the browser drops, leaving the panes stuck. Widening the divider from 7px to 25px makes the degenerate case marginally more reachable. A `track <= 0` bail (or `Number.isFinite` guard) would keep the clamp honest.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. Enforcement is now the default (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31) and PushPull with verb `rw` is the write gate that denies a share-link viewer (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:334, 370; READ_GATED_METHODS is only AttachDocument at :108). The change silences read-only presence for PDF (pdf-collab.tsx:134) and slides (slides-view.tsx:1137) citing exactly this wedging failure, but the spreadsheet path has no equivalent guard: shared-document.tsx:181,283 mounts SheetView read-only for a viewer inside the sheet-* DocumentProvider (:1018-1025); sheet-view.tsx:1012 builds `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId)` unconditionally; the constructor publishes presence immediately (yorkie-store.ts:86-88) and updateSelection republishes on every selection change (yorkie-store.ts:628-634) with no readOnly awareness anywhere in that file. The engine path is reachable for a viewer: sheet.ts:3075-3080 setActiveCell -> syncSelectionToPresence -> ensureAxisOrder (3029, a document-root write) and updateSelection (3045, 3058); sheet.ts has no readOnly checks, and worksheet.ts:3970,3988,3990 invoke selectEnd/addSelection/selectStart from mousedown without a read-only gate (the nearby readOnly guards at 3448/3457/3469/3511 cover freeze/resize/hidden/drag-move only). So a viewer gets 403'd on mount and on any cursor move, wedging sync — a crash-equivalent break of a core flow. No not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies; it is squarely a correctness/missing-guard defect.

finding.summary: Read-only PDF mount still writes presence on every page change, which enforcement (now the default) refuses at PushPull
finding.evidence: `onActivePageChange` does `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` with no `readOnly` guard, and it is wired unconditionally into `PdfViewer` (`renderPageOverlay`/`onActivePageChange` at line 310) for both the owner and the share route. This is exactly the reasoning the diff itself applies 60 lines above to justify `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`: a local change on a read-only mount is carried by the next `PushPull`, whose verb is derived from the change pack, so it arrives as `rw` and `hasAccess()` refuses it for a share-link `viewer` (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:322`, `link.role === 'editor'`). A presence-only change is still a change in the pack. `packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:513-520` records that a viewer's `sync()` carrying a local change comes back `PermissionDenied`. Before this diff that was latent (shadow mode allowed everything unless an operator opted in); with enforcement as the default, a viewer-role PDF share link that merely *scrolls* now gets its sync denied, so comments stop flowing for it. The seed was fixed and the presence write in the same file was not.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that `onActivePageChange` writes presence "with no `readOnly` guard" — is false in this working tree. `packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:134` reads `if (readOnly || !doc || pageIndex === lastPageRef.current) return;` before the `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` at :136, and lines 122-131 document precisely the PushPull/`rw`/viewer-denial rationale the reviewer says was omitted. The guard covers the actor named in the finding: `shared-document.tsx:699` derives `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` and passes it at :709 into `PdfCollabProvider`, which forwards it to `PdfCollabStateProvider` at pdf-collab.tsx:217; the owner route passes `readOnly={false}` (file-detail.tsx:94), which is the mount that should publish. I enumerated every call site of the protected operation: the handler is created only at pdf-collab.tsx:133, exposed at :162, consumed at :299, passed to `PdfViewer` at :319, and invoked via `onActive` at pdf-viewer.tsx:183 — all routed through the same guarded closure. A repo-wide grep for `activePage`/`p.set(` shows no other presence write on the PDF path. With no unguarded write, the claimed chain (local change in pack -> verb `rw` -> `hasAccess()` refusal for a viewer -> wedged sync) never begins, so there is no correctness defect here.

finding.summary: Slides (and board) viewer mounts publish presence on navigation/selection — the same denied-PushPull path the diff closed for notes
finding.evidence: `broadcast()` calls `store.updatePresence({ activeSlideId, selectedElementIds, selectedTableCells })` and is subscribed to `editor.onCurrentSlideChange` / `onSelectionChange` / `onCellSelectionChange` (lines 1149-1151) with no `readOnly` gate, so a viewer-role share link changing slides emits a presence-only local change. `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:593-597` has the same unguarded `store.updatePresence` on selection change (only the *cursor* publisher is gated by `if (!readOnly)` at line 538). By the diff's own argument (`pdf-collab.tsx:191-201`, `read-only.ts:57-67`) such a change is pushed as verb `rw` and refused for a viewer, and the notes path was deliberately neutered (`readOnlyNoteStore` covers `setLocalSelection`) for precisely this reason. Making enforcement the default turns these into live denials on any deployment that registered `PushPull`. Confidence is low only because I could not confirm from the repo whether a read-only slides/board mount actually emits those callbacks.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the slides and board presence publishers call store.updatePresence on slide/selection change with "no readOnly gate". Both are in fact gated. In slides-view.tsx the broadcast() closure subscribed to onSelectionChange/onCurrentSlideChange/onCellSelectionChange (lines 1157-1159) begins with `if (readOnlyMount) return;` (line 1137) before the store.updatePresence at 1143, where readOnlyMount is derived from the prop at line 198. In board-view.tsx the selection listener is `editor.onSelectionChange(() => { if (readOnly) return; store.updatePresence(...) })` at lines 600-605 — the finding's assertion that only the cursor publisher is gated (line 538) is wrong; line 538 gates the pointer listeners and line 601 independently gates the selection publisher. Both files also carry comments (slides 1130-1135, board 594-599) articulating exactly the PushPull/verb-rw rationale the finding says was ignored. The read-only mount path supplies the flag: shared-document.tsx:397 passes readOnly to BoardView and shared-document.tsx:502-503 passes readOnly to SlidesView, so the guard's input is actually set for share-link viewers. The described ungated code does not exist as claimed.
